b2-LGF-B:
Mitochondrial & cellular energy starvation (glutamine, butyrate, TCA intermediates): your gut barrier needs a lot of energy to keep the tight junctions intact, and it needs it right away, right there in the gut lining. If your enterocytes (small intestine) or colonocytes (large intestine) go without the fuels their mitochondria prefer, the barrier physically falls apart, which lets lipopolysaccharides (LPS) and endotoxins leak into your bloodstream.
L-Glutamine (watch Dr. Rhonda vid) is the main fuel for enterocytes, and for activated immune cells too. It skips the complex digestive steps and turns directly into alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG) inside the mitochondria, where it powers the citric acid cycle. That immediate energy hit to the cells is what drives the repair of the gut mucosal barrier, and it prevents LPS from leaking through. Take 5g a day as a baseline to counter the gut mucosal breakdown you get from high-intensity or high-volume training (like CrossFit or intense cardio). During acute immune exposure or high systemic stress, work up to 10-30g a day. Same if you're dealing with active IBD (Crohn's/Colitis).
CAUTION: fast-multiplying cancer cells can also hijack glutamine to fuel their rapid replication. So if you have an active colon or liver malignancy right now, avoid the high-dose glutamine titrations (the liver sees it first, since the portal vein delivers it there).
Butyrate & SCFAs: the small intestine runs on glutamine, while the large intestine relies on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate, as I mentioned under diverticulosis. You can get these from raw resistant starch fermentation or your home-brewed SIBO yogurt, and they fuel your colonocytes and seal up the lower gut barrier. They also systematically suppress inflammatory signals.
TCA cycle intermediates (malic & citric acid): organic acids like malate and citrate feed directly into the exact same mitochondrial energy pathways as glutamine. You can take organic malic acid, or eat clean sour foods like tart cherries or green apples. Either way your gut epithelial cells get a rapid, alternative fuel, which speeds up mucosal healing from a different biochemical angle.
b2-ST1-B:
Optional Ready-Made Gut Stacks
I don't think there's a universal supplement stack that heals everyone's gut. And the right order still matters: you fix the digestion mechanics first, then reset diet and motility, and you only escalate into antimicrobial or anti-parasite protocols if symptoms persist after that.
But some people would rather have a ready-made starting point than buy every ingredient separately. For a general "repair and rebuild" approach, I'd look for a stack that covers three categories:
Microbiome support: a well-tolerated probiotic or probiotic system
Prebiotic / butyrate support: something that helps short-chain fatty acid production, esp. butyrate
Barrier repair: nutrients that support the gut lining, such as glutamine, zinc carnosine, colostrum, mucosal-support herbs, or similar compounds (the first three are all under Leaky gut, above)
b2-ST2-B:
The next three kits were actually Gemini's suggestions, but so far they're the best ones I've seen, tho I haven't used them myself. You can check their reviews. For a general stack, Microbiome Labs Total Gut Restoration is the best of the bunch, because it combines probiotic and prebiotic components, plus mucosal support. For a more leaky-gut-specific stack, Dr. Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit is a reasonable option. And if you want a single gut-lining repair formula, Designs for Health GI Revive is one of the more complete products, but think of it as a repair product, which is only one piece of a full gut protocol.
I wouldn't recommend general "gut cleanse" stacks built around oregano oil, wormwood, black walnut, berberine or other antimicrobial herbs as a universal starting point. Those belong later in the decision tree, when there's a stronger reason to suspect overgrowth, parasites, H. pylori, or some other specific problem. (My own advice is different for H. pylori, where berberine works well: see Parasites, above.)
Whatever you take, start low, especially with prebiotics, resistant starch, butyrate-support products and probiotics. If you have severe pain, GI bleeding, fever, dehydration or rapid weight loss, work with a qualified clinician instead of stacking supplements on your own. Same goes for active IBD flares, cancer, immune suppression, pregnancy, or complex medical conditions.
